Commentary.Commentary: Right then. Both the skippers get together and pose with the trophy as the series ended in a 1-1 draw. Sri Lanka would be pleased with their effort and end their final home Test game of the year on a high and they have reclaimed their spot in the top three of the ICC World Test Championship points table. They will now shift their attention to the T20 World Cup Group Stage to get their ticket for the main event. They will face Namibia on 16th October. For Pakistan though, they head out to the Netherlands for an ODI series which will begin on the 16th of August. Hope you enjoyed our coverage. Until next time, take care and goodbye!

Dimuth Karunaratane, the skipper of Sri Lanka says his back is still not right and he will get an MRI tomorrow. He says that when Angelo Mathews got out he felt like he had to bat positively and put pressure on Pakistan. He adds that as a team they are playing well and the batters and bowlers are contributing equally. He says there were some mistakes in the past that cost them matches but they try to learn from them and execute their plans better. He praises Prabhath Jayasuriya and says that he knew his potential and that's why Prabath was given the opportunity and flourished with it. He ends by saying that it is a great achievement to play 100 Test matches for Mathews and he has been playing with him since U-15. Adds that he hopes Mathews can play many more matches for Sri Lanka.

Babar Azam, the Pakistani, skipper in for a chat. He starts by saying it was tough for them to win the series. Adds that their batting wasn't up to the mark and that hurt them the most. Mentions that Dhananjaya de Silva's innings was the biggest difference in the game. Also mentions that they will take a lot of positives from this series and hopes to improve their game in the future.

Prabath Jayasuriya is the PLAYER OF THE SERIES for picking up 17 wickets across the two Test matches. He says that he worked hard and was patient for his chance and is happy with his performance. He adds that the surface was not that easy and it was more about the partnership in bowling and waiting for the wickets to fall and then putting more pressure by bowling on the right line and lengths. He ends by saying that he had a lot of support from his family and players and is delighted with the win and will look to continue this form.

Dhananjaya de Silva, who was the acting captain for Sri Lanka for almost all of the Test match, wins the Man of the Match award for his incredible ton. He starts by saying he is really happy after getting a ton after almost 13 innings. Also praises the effort of the boys in all departments. Mentions, he had worked on himself a lot, also there is the added pressure when a batsman doesn't score but he could handle the pressure. Ends by saying that being the stand-in captain is a good challenge for him.
The presentation ceremony...

Early in the game, Dimuth Karunaratne won the toss and opted to bat first and his side put on a sizeable score on the back of contributions throughout the batting order. Naseem Shah and Yasir Shah both bowled well with the young pacer showing good control. Then, the Lankan bowling attack led by a five-wicket haul of Ramesh Mendis bundled out the opposition for just 231 runs, handing the hosts a big lead of 147 runs. Only Agha Salman showed some fight as he brought up his maiden half-century. Pakistan did make early inroads in the second innings but soon the bowlers proved to be ineffective and the stand-in captain for Sri Lanka, Dhananjaya de Silva scored a ton to ensure his side had a lead of over 500 runs. Sri Lanka looked in control but when almost the entirety of the final session on Day 4 was called off due to bad light, it seemed that luck was against them. On Day 5 though, it was a completely different story and the hosts ended up winning the match comfortably by 246 runs. Stay tuned for the presentation ceremony.

Pakistan had the lead in the series after an immaculate run chase in the first Test match but their in-form batters have certainly disappointed in the second Test. Both openers were found vulnerable to the conditions and even though Babar Azam played well in the second innings, the first innings deficit made a huge difference in the game. Pakistan started Day 5 on a negative note having lost Imam-ul-Haq early but then the skipper and vice-captain put on a good stand. It was then Rizwan's misjudgment that created the opening for the opposition and the Run-Out of Fawad Alam only made things worse. After Lunch, it got very nervy and the middle order just was driven through as only Yasir Shah got a few boundaries. All in all, a disappointing end for the visitors as they had a great chance of getting an away Test series win and have dropped down to fifth position on the ICC World Test Championship points table.

This has been a memorable comeback from Sri Lanka after going 1-0 down in this two-match Test series. What a turnaround this has been on Day 5 with bad light and dark clouds taking overs off Sri Lanka's hand, but they remained resolute and got the win. After a bit of a sedate first hour on Day 5, Prabath Jayasuriya started to turn the tide in favor of his side. Then Ramesh Mendis joined him and the pair picked up nine wickets in between them with Jayasuriya picking up a fourth five-wicket haul in just three Test matches. In the absence of Dimuth Karunaratne for most of the game, vice-captain Dhananjaya de Silva led the side extremely well and they deserved the win completely. Angelo Mathews also ends his 100th Test match with a win.

What a game of Test cricket we have witnessed! Sri Lanka dominated almost all 5 Days but the game just started to drift away from them late on Day 4 and early on Day 5. Their spinners though have done a remarkable job when it mattered most and the hosts have indeed leveled the series. Pakistan put up a fight but that was only for a short time and they have been outclassed here. With that result, Galle keeps up with its reputation of being a ground where there is a team that ends up on the winning side.

OUT! TAKEN! Mendis gets the last man and the Sri Lankans are delighted and there are celebratory scenes all over the ground. This is floated and on off, turning in, Naseem Shah tries to go for the big shot across the line again but this time mistimes his shot. The ball goes high in the air towards Dunith Wellalage who is stationed at deep mid-wicket judges it well and pouches it safely. Sri Lanka win the game by 246 runs.
Commentary.Howout: c Dunith Wellalage b Ramesh Mendis

Commentary.Commentary: Full again on off, turning in. Shah knocks it to the off side.
FOUR! A gift from Mendis. This is a full toss and on off, Shah smashes it through extra covers for a boundary.
Floated on off, turning in sharply, Shah is caught in his crease but manages to defend it well.
Tossed up on middle, Shah comes down the track to loft it over mid-wicket but gets an inside edge and it goes towards short leg.
Flighted on off, turning in, Shah blocks it onto the pitch.
Full and off, pushed to covers.
Looped up, outside off, turns in a touch. Ali stays back and tries to punch it away but misses. It goes to fine leg after hitting the pads.
Fuller, down leg. Shah clips it to square leg for a single.
Darted on the pads, Shah goes back and flicks it to mid-wicket.
This one comes in with the arm, full and on middle, blocked out solidly.
Tossed up, on the stumps. Shah defends it out.
Maiden over by Mendis. This is tossed up around off, Ali keeps it out.
Flighted delivery and on middle, angling in, Ali goes for defense but inside edges it past short leg.
Flighted on middle, turning away, Ali blocks it with his outer half to the off side.
Shortish and outside off, Ali stays back and punches it to silly point.
Tossed up full and on middle, Nauman Ali pushes it back to the bowler.
Floated full and on middle, Nauman Ali knocks it to silly point.
Fuller, outside off, turns away a touch. Shah gets it to point off the outer half.
SIX! BANG! Fuller, on off. Shah offers full face of the bat and tonks it over the long on fence for a biggie.
Slower through the air, full and on off. Shah blocks it out watchfully.
On off, defended out.
Floated and full, on fourth stump. Shah looks to defend it out but gets beaten on the outside edge.
Outside off, left alone.
Pushed through quicker onto the pads, Shah tickles it to fine leg for one.
SIX! Shah is trying to attack. This is flighted and full on off, Naseem Shah makes room and smokes it over extra covers for a biggie.
Shah living on the edge here. This is tossed up on middle, Naseem Shah goes for the big shot but gets an inside edge onto his pads.
BEATEN! This floated around off, Naseem Shah goes for the block but is beaten on the outside edge.
Flighted on middle, turning in, Naseem Shah pads it away. It looks close and there is an appeal for LBW but turned down.
Naseem Shah is the last man in for Pakistan.

OUT! DRAGGED ON! Another man bites the dust for Pakistan. Mendis gets his third wicket now. It is full and on off. Ali looks to sweep it away but does not connect. It hits him on the pads, might've got some arm on it as well, as he goes through with the shot. It goes onto disturb the bails. Sri Lanka need just a wicket now.
Fuller, on off, Ali blocks it back to the bowler.
Nauman Ali is the new man in.

OUT! CAUGHT! Prabath Jayasuriya picks up his fifth wicket of the innings. He has been consistent for the hosts throughout this series. Yasir Shah's cameo comes to an end. It is tossed up, around middle and leg, drifting in. Shah tries to flick it away but is a tad early into his shot. It takes the leading edge and goes to gully. Kusal Mendis takes a sitter. Sri Lanka now need two more wickets to win the game.
Commentary.Howout: c Kusal Mendis b Prabath Jayasuriya

Commentary.Commentary: Four dots on the trot! Fuller, outside off. Shah drives it to mid off.
Fuller, on the pads, clipped to short leg.
A bit flatter and around off, Shah keeps it out towards silly point.
Around middle, Shah gets a big stride forward to defend.
SIX! BANG! It is tossed up, full and outside off. Ali lofts it overs the bowler's head for a biggie.
On off, defended on the front foot.
Fuller, on middle, defended out solidly.
FOUR! Boundaries are flowing for Pakistan. It is full, going down leg. Ali tickles it fine. It races away to the fine leg boundary.
Fuller, around off, defended out.
On off, blocked out.
Very full and on middle, driven towards mid off.
Drifted onto the pads, trying to turn it away from there. Yasir Shah nudges it off the inside edge and though leg slip for a couple of runs.
Sliding into the pads, Shah keeps it out.
A bit of drift again into the right-hander, Shah negates it well.
FOUR! Deft touch! Full and floated on the pads, Shah with a fine tickle this time and the ball runs away into the fine leg fence.
On the bounce! Nice bit of drift into middle and leg, Yasir Shah pushes at it with soft hands and the ball lands just in front of the man at silly point.
Around off again, Shah looks to drive but gets it off the inside edge and towards backward square leg for a single.
Quicker and flatter, turning it in from outside off. Yasir Shah watchfully keeps it out.
Fuller and around off, Shah makes the block.
FOUR! Yasir Shah dealing in just boundaries at the moment. On a length and around middle, Shah gets a big stride forward and sweeps it hard, through mid-wicket for yet another boundary.

FOUR! That is a shot of real confidence and it looks like Yasir Shah wants to give a bit of stick back to the bowlers. Tossed up, around middle, Shah dances down the track and lofts it one-bounce into the mid-wicket fence.
A tad shorter and on the pads, Hasan Ali works it 'round the corner for a single.
Tosses it up again, drawing the batter forward. This is outside off, Shah drives it gently towards extra cover.
Much better from Jayasuriya. Flighted, close to the off pole and turning away sharply. Yasir Shah plays inside the line of the ball.
FOUR! A third boundary in the over and Yasir Shah enjoying his stay at the crease for now. Tossed up, full and on off, Shah pummels it uppishly and through mid on for a boundary.
FOUR! Just a bit too full and too straight from Jayasuriya. This is on leg stump, Yasir Shah drives it through wide mid on and picks up yet another boundary.
On a nagging length, on off and turning away, Shah prods forward to defend.
FOUR! Full and on middle and leg, Yasir Shah decides to have a crack at it and heaves it in front of mid-wicket and collects a boundary.
Tossed up, around off, Ali strides forward to make the block. A wicket maiden them for Ramesh Mendis!
Looped up, full and on off, turning in, Hasan Ali keeps it out towards short leg.
Hasan Ali is the new man in.

OUT! CAUGHT! This is poor cricket from Mohammad Nawaz, he just didn't have the temperament to defend and pays the price. This is floated up very full and around middle, turning away a touch. Nawaz tries to go for the big shot, against the turn and ends up slicing it high. The ball loops up around the cover region where Dinesh Chandimal takes a simple catch. The deadly duo of Jayasuriya and Mendis doing the job here for Sri Lanka who are now three wickets away from victory.
Commentary.Howout: c Dinesh Chandimal b Ramesh Mendis

Commentary.Commentary: Nice bit of drift into the off stump, Nawaz watchfully keeps it out.

A appeal for stumping! This could be close. Tossed up, outside off. It grips and turns away. Nawaz tries to defend inside the line but misses. Niroshan Dickwella collects and clips the bails quickly. The umpire takes it upstairs to confirm. The UltraEdge show no bat is involved. The side-on angled shows that Nawaz had his back foot grounded. The final decision is NOT OUT.
This is angled into middle from around the stumps, kept out by Nawaz.

Peach of a delivery to end the over! This is floated up, on a fuller length and closer to the off pole. The ball grips and turns away to beat the outside edge. The keeper whips off the bails and appeals for a stumping. The decision is sent upstairs but the replay shows that Yasir Shah has his back foot firmly planted inside the crease. NOT OUT!

Is that stumped? The square leg umpire takes it upstairs to confirm! The UlraEdge shows no bat is involved. The side-on angle shows that Shah had his back leg grounded and the big screen shows NOT OUT.
On middle, pushed away towards mid on.
Tosses it up, full and wide, Yasir Shah thrashes it past the man at silly point.
Yasir Shah is the new man in.

OUT! LBW! Prabath Jayasuriya's dream run continues in the Test format. This might just be the wicket that seals the game for Sri Lanka. Flights this one, around middle and off and on a nagging length. Babar Azam presses forward to defend but misses and gets pinged in front. There is a huge appeal for an LBW and the finger is raised! Babar Azam reviews it right away and frankly speaking, he doesn't have any other option. UltraEdge shows there's no bat involved and Ball Tracking shows that the ball is hitting the top of middle. Sri Lanka are just four wickets away now from leveling the series.
Flighted, on a length and around off, Babar defends it off the front foot.
Turning down leg and keeping a bit low, Babar Azam works it 'round the corner and down towards fine leg for a couple.

A huge appeal for lbw but the umpire is unmoved. It is looped up, around middle, sliding in. Nawaz tries to cut it away but it looks like he inside-edges it onto the pads. Dhananjaya de Silva opts against the review. Although the replays later suggest that it was pad first.
On off, defended out.
FOUR! Nicely played! It is short, outside off. Nawaz cuts it hard through covers for a boundary.
Tossed up, outside off. Nawaz chases it but misses.
This is angled into the pads, on a fuller length. Nawaz blocks it out on his front foot.
A dot to start the over! It is tossed up, around off, turning away a touch. Nawaz covers the stumps and leaves it alone.
Tossed up outside off, turning further away, Babar Azam leaves it alone.

Oh, this is really close! This is the arm ball and outside off, Babar Azam goes for the drive through covers but plays all over it. The ball goes just past the inside edge to the keeper. A rare loose shot from Babar and it was inches away from hitting the stumps.
Loopy delivery on off, driftin in, Babar Azam blocks it out.
On off, kept out.
Flatter delivery around off, Nawaz pushes it towards covers for one.

EDGED BUT DROPPED! This is nicely tossed up on middle, turns away a bit, Babar Azam leans on for the block but gets an outside edge towards the first slip. DDS there reacts late and dives to his left but cannot grab it. The ball goes towards short fine leg and the batter gets a run. Another let off for Babar.
Floated on off, Mohammad Nawaz makes room but hits it straight to short covers.
On middle, blocked.
FOUR! Good hit! This is tossed up full and on middle and leg, Mohammad Nawaz clears his front leg and smashes it towards the long on fence for a boundary.
Flighted on middle, Mohammad Nawaz knocks it to the leg side with the inner half of his bat.
Short and outside off, Mohammad Nawaz cuts it past point for a brace.
Short ball, outside off. Nawaz cuts it to point but straight to the fielder.
Fuller, outside off. Nawaz pushes it to cover for one.
Looped up, outside off. Mohammad Nawaz tries to defends it on his front foot but misses. It lobs off his pads to the left of the keeper.
On middle, flicked to mid-wicket for one.
Ah! This is close! It is full and around off. Azam comes down the track and yorks himself. He tries to drive it away but misses. The ball stays very low as it goes to the keeper.
On middle, defended back to the bowler.
Shrp turn! It drifts in, pitches on leg and turns away off the deck. Azam leaves it alone.
Mendis bowls the arm ball, on middle and angling in, Mohammad Nawaz is caught in his crease and only manages to knock it back to the bowler.
Quicker and flatter on off, Nawaz defends it on the back foot.
Floated around off, turning in a bit, Mohammad Nawaz pads it away. The fielders appeal for the LBW but the finger stays down. This looked close.
Sligthly short and on middle, Mohammad Nawaz punches it of his back foot to mid on.
Tossed up on middle, Nawaz plays a front foot defense.
Mendis starts with a shorter one and on the leg side, Babar Azam tucks it through square leg for one.
It is going to be Ramesh Mendis to continue with his off-spin from the other end.
A bit short and outside off, Mohammad Nawaz stays back and knocks it to the off side.
On middle, blocked out.

Flighted on middle, turning in, Mohammad Nawaz tries to defend it but gets hit on the pads and the ball loops and goes into the hands of short leg. There is a sltiffled appeal for catch but turned down.
Tossed up on off, turning in, Mohammad Nawaz blocks it out.
Prabath Jayasuriya starts witha ripper after the break. This is floated around off, holds its line, Mohammad Nawaz goes to play it for the turn but misses it completely.

We are back for the afternoon session on Day 5! The umpires and the Sri Lankan players are out in the middle. Babar Azam is set to his resume his stay at the crease and will now be joined by Mohammad Nawaz. Prabath Jayasuriya is all set to complete his unfinished over.
... Day 5, Session 2 ...

Sri Lanka have made a great comeback in this session and surely they would now be aiming to get the remaining wickets as quickly as possible. The hosts need to keep the conditions in mind and need to be on the money in the afternoon session. Ashita Fernando bowled just a few overs but it was mainly their spinner working in tandem and doing the trick for them. Prabath Jayasuriya took a couple of wicket while Mendis got one. Sri Lanka also looked solid in the field and they hardly made any mistakes. Sri Lanka will be itching to get back on the field now with the momentum on their side. Will they be able to end things in the post-Lunch session? To find out, join us at 12.40 pm IST (7.10 am GMT).

The visitors came out with an intention to bat throughtout the day, but they find themselves in a precarious position at Lunch on Day 5. They ended up losing 4 wickets in this morning session. Imam-ul-Haq departed early in the morning although later, Azam and Rizwan managed to stable their innings with a solid stand of 79 runs. Things though started to fall apart once Rizwan departed. Fawad Alam and Agha Salman were sent back cheaply and Babar Azam now holds the key for the visitors. Even he could've been back in the hut, if the review hadn't saved him.

Well, how quickly things change in a Test match. It looked like Pakistan were well in control of their innings, but they've been caught napping in the final 30 minutes of the morning session and without a doubt Sri Lanka will be the happier side going into the break.

OUT! TAKEN! Brilliant reflex catch by Kusal Mendis at short leg to send Agha Salman back in the hut. This is tossed up full and on middle, Agha Salman goes down to get inside the line and tries to paddle it away behind square but little did he know that Kusal Mendis already anticipated the shot and started moving to his right before the shot has been played. It is hit firmly but Mendis shows quick reflexes and grabs it with both hands. A huge moment in the game and Sri Lanka are right on top. With that, the umpires have called for LUNCH ON DAY 5.
Commentary.Howout: c Kusal Mendis b Prabath Jayasuriya

Commentary.Commentary: Full and outside off, Babar Azam leans on and pushes it to covers.
Gives it some air this time, turning away a bit, Babar Azam keeps it out well.
Tossed up on middle, Babar Azam blocks it out.
A bit short and on the leg stump line, Babar Azam pushes it to mid-wicket.
Flighted on middle, turning in a bit too much, Babar Azam works it to leg slip.
Floated but down the leg, Babar Azam tucks it to the leg side.
FOUR! Confidently played! Tossed up on off, Agha Salman dances down the track and drives it straight back past the bowler to collect a boundary.
Turning down leg, Babar tucks it away towards fine leg for a single.

That was almost catchable height as well! This is drifted onto the pads, Babar Azam flicks it to the right of the man at short leg who sticks out a right hand but can't reach it. The batters get a couple of runs as the ball goes towards deep backward square leg.
Tossed up on off, Babar Azam has a tentative push at it and the ball goes uppishly yet again but well past silly mid off.
On middle, kept out by Babar.

Uppish but safe! Babar Azam is playing shots that are against his general style of play. This is floated up outside off and turning away, Babar with an aggressive cover drive but slices it. Luckily for him, the ball loops up and falls safely around the point region.

Is there an inside edge? If yes then another chance goes abegging. It is tossed up, full and on off. Agha Salman tries to block it away but it lobs in front of him. Oshada Fernando dives in front of him from short leg but is unable to get to the ball. The replays later show that there was an inside edge onto the pads. A lucky escape for Agha Salman.
Tossed up on off, spins in sharply again, Agha Salman defends it close to his body. Ramesh Mendis bowling really well here.
Pitched up on off, Agha Salman knocks it to the leg side.

A huge appeal for LBW but turned down. This is floated on off, turn in sharply, Agha Salman goes for the block but gets hit on the front pad. The fielders appeal for the LBW but the finger stays down.
Agha Salman walks out to bat with Pakistan under a bit of pressure.

OUT! RUN OUT! Horrible mix up in the middle and Alam has to go back. This is floated full on middle, Fawad Alam uses his feet and drives it towards mid on and calls for the run straightaway. Babar Azam responds to him but is caught ball watching here. The skipper is too late to send his partner back. Alam has nowhere to go as he is left stranded in the middle of the pitch. The fielder throws the ball to the keeper and Niroshan Dickwella does the rest, as Alam is forced to continue his run back to the dressing room.
On off, kept out.
Yet another probing over from Prabath Jayasuriya, goes hunting for the front pad but Babar Azam does well to keep it out.
Half an appeal but Babar Azam way down the track. This is angled into leg stump, Babar dances down the track but gets beten in flight. The ball crashes into the pads and rolls away towards gully.
Short and on off, punched to covers.
Tossed up on off, turning away a bit, Babar Azam blocks it with outer half towards silly point.

Good comeback delivery by Prabath Jayasuriya. This is slower through the air and on middle, angling in, Babar Azam leans forward to defend but plays down the wrong line and gets hit on the pads. The Sri Lankans appeal for the LBW but the umpire is not interested. DDS opts for the review. UltraEdge shows no bat involved and the Ball tracking shows it is missing the wickets. Sri Lanka lose their review.
FOUR! Lovely shot! This is tossed up on off, Babar Azam dances down the track and flicks it towards the deep mid-wicket fence for a boundary.
Short and outside off, Fawad Alam plays it off the back foot towards backward point.
BEATEN! Floated up, around off and just turning away a bit but sharply. Fawad Alam presents a dead bat at it but gets beaten past the outside edge.
Tossed up, around off, this is pushed away onto the off side.
Around middle, pushed away to mid on.

Fawad Alam escapes three types of dismissals in a single delivery. Mendis drifts this one in full and on middle, turning it away, Fawad Alam manages to get his front leg just out of the way and keeps it down to silly point. Fawad though falls over a bit and almost gets run out.
Ramesh Mendis comes from around the wicket and serves it full and around off, Fawad keeps it out.
Nicely drifted onto middle, Babar keeps it out. End of an excellent over from Prabath Jayasuriya.
Leading edge but safe! Flighted, around off and just turning away a touch. Babar looks to block but gets a leading edge that falls safely around the vacant silly point region.
Excellent fielding! Drops it a bit short and around off, Babar Azam punches it off the back foot but the fielder at extra cover makes a good diving stop.
Comes from over the wicket to the left-hander and serves a very full ball around middle. Fawad Alam reaches out well and sweeps it behind square on the leg side to get off the mark with a single.
Fawad Alam comes out to the middle now.

OUT! Cleaned up! A huge, huge misjudgment from Mohammad Rizwan and he has handed an opportunity to Sri Lanka to get back in the game. Prabath Jayasuriya angles this one in on a nagging length and very close to the off stump. Rizwan strides forward and leaves the ball expecting the turn. The ball though goes straight on with the arm, brushes the off pole and the bail comes off. The keeper pouches the ball and goes up in excitement as he knows what has happened. The umpires go upstairs and the side-on replay shows that the ball just clipped the outside of the off stump. Jayasuriya has done it again for his team.
Is that out? The umpire takes it upstairs to confirm if the ball has his the stumps. The replays confirm that and the big screen shows OUT.
Drifted on the pads, this is tucked away behind square on the leg side for a couple of runs.
Just a tad short and turning down leg, left alone by Babar.
On a length, around off, this is pushed away towards mid on.
A bit quicker and darted onto off, Babar Azam rocks back to make the block.
Much better from the bowler. Gives it a bit of flight and bowls it on middle, Babar looks to defend off the front foot and does so towards short leg.
On the shorter side and turning into leg, Mohammad Rizwan has enough time to rock back and ease it towards square leg for a run.
Drifted onto the pads, Rizwan nudges it towards leg slip.

Massive turn! Drifts it in from outside off and the ball just grips and turns square, leaving the batter bamboozled. The ball zips past the outside edge and there is half an appeal from behind the stumps as well.
Just teasing the batter to go for the drive, tossed up, around off, Babar Azam looks for the cover drive but checks his shot and just slices it towards point.
And again! On middle, Babar leans forward and keeps it out.
Nicely flighted, around middle, Babar defends it off the front foot.
Nagging length, angling into middle, Babar gets behind the line of the ball to make the block.
Starts off with a floater around off, Babar Azam presses forward well and keeps it out on the off side.
Change. Prabath Jayasuriya (19-2-72-1) is back into the attack now.
Goes a bit fuller and angles it onto middle and leg, Babar works it through mid on for one more.
TWO BYES! This is poor from Ramesh Mendis, shorter and turning well down leg, the ball beats everyone and goes towards fine leg. The batters race back for two.
Darted into middle and leg, Babar keeps it out.
Keeps it on a shorter length and Babar pulls it past the man at short leg fora couple of runs.
Short again, turning down leg, worked away in between short leg and leg slip for a single.
Mendis starts off the new spell with a shortish delivery, turning into the pads, Rizwan goes on the back foot to dab it down towards short leg.
Fuller, on middle and leg. Azam defends it back to the bowler.
Slightly short, outside off. Azam goes back and cuts it through point. Two runs taken.
Fuller, on off. Azam tries to clip it past mid on but finds the fielder.
Darted on the pads, Rizwan flicks it to the right of mid on. The batters are quick to cross.
It is full, on middle and leg, drifting in. Mohammad Rizwan blocks it out.

The morning session is set to begin. Both the umpire make their way on the field. Followed by Babar Azam and Imam-ul-Haq who walk out with their blades. Sri Lanka are seen to be in a huddle before they spread out on the field. It will be Asitha Fernando to start with the ball.

PITCH REPORT - Russel Arnold says that there is nothing much to report new here as it is still dry. There was overnight rain but the groundstaff has managed to keep it dry, although there are a few scratches. He adds that the batters will feel confident to survive on it as it has slowed down and it will be slightly easier to negotiate spin.

Chris Silverwood, the head coach of Sri Lanka is in for a chat.. He says they cannot predict the weather, but all they though about how quick can they bowl out Pakistan and though accordingly. Mentions, the bowlers need to maintain their lines and lengths. Adds that it is a basic rule but still holds a lot of importance. Says that DDS wanted to score runs and get into his groove and this one was a timely innings under immense pressure. Adds that the side is progressing really well and seems to be on the right track. Ends by syaing it is a real privilege for him to be here in this position.

For Pakistan, the equation is pretty simple, as it would be a bit too much to expect the batters to chase down a steep target in a single day. Pakistan will be aiming to build solid stands in the middle and bat throughout the day to win the series. It won't be an easy task though, against a talented bowling side of Sri Lanka, who impressed in the first innings, and they will be backing themselves to do something similar. Can Sri Lanka pick up early wickets in the morning session? Or will Pakistan remain unscathed till Lunch? Stick around to find out how things pan out.

Hello and a warm welcome to the final day of the second Test match between Sri Lanka and Pakistan. The hosts have their noses clearly in front in this race, although things surely did not go as they would've envisioned them. They need 9 wickets to level the series.
... Day 5, Session 1 ...

Right then, a lot of overs have been lost on Day 4, around 25 overs in total and that will certainly have a prominent impact on the outcome of the game. The game seems to be heading towards a draw from the offset but Sri Lanka will believe that if they get Babar and Imam early on, then the middle order of Pakistan is quite fragile. Pakistan though will be determined to make use of the help they have been given by the conditions and see the day out. Join us for a riveting final day and the first ball will be bowled at 9.45 am IST (4.15 am GMT). Our build-up though will begin much sooner. Cheers!

Pakistan have been second best throughout this game but what they did in the fourth innings of the previous game has helped them here too. The opposition had to bat for a prolonged period of time because of the mental advantage that Pakistan had and the visitors themselves have so far batted pretty well in the chase. Skipper Babar Azam and Imam-ul-Haq are the two batters in good nick and they will be feeling if they negotiate the morning session on Day 5 well, they can draw the game and seal the series victory.

Sri Lanka opted not to declare at Lunch and then played for some more time after the interval and this additional time taken in declaration might cost them dearly. The hosts managed to pick up only one wicket in the afternoon session and with just six overs being completed in the final session before the players had to go off, the Lankan bowlers haven't had much of a chance to make inroads before the end of Day 4. It will now require a big effort from their bowlers early on Day 5 to have a chance of getting the win.

Unfortunately, the scenes from the ground show that after bad light stopped play, there was a massive dark cloud hovering over the ground and Stumps have been officially called. Day 4 has provided many twists and turns in the game and whilst the opening session belonged to Sri Lanka, at the moment, a draw looks the likeliest of outcomes. The hosts were cruising early in the day but given what happened in the last game, they had to ensure they got a lead of over 500 runs in order to shut down Pakistan from having a sniff of winning the game but that has backfired.

UPDATE 4.20 pm IST (10.50 am GMT) - Still no official word from the ground. Given play was stopped around this time last evening, Stumps looming large at the moment. And if that happens, then Pakistan will be breathing a huge sigh of relief but the hosts will just get more and more frustrated by it. Stay tuned for further updates.

The two umpires are in a discussion now and the Pakistani batters are already walking towards the pavilion. After the long discussion, the umpires decide that it is time to go off! Pakistan have been aided by bad light and Sri Lanka will be kicking themselves at the moment. For now, the play has been suspended due to bad light. Also, the covers are on too as there is a chance of a shower as well. Stay tuned for further updates.

We are back for the final session on Day 4! The two umpires are out on the field and so are the Sri Lankan players. Imam-ul-Haq and Babar Azam are set to resume their stay at the crease. It will be Ramesh Mendis who will start proceedings with the ball after the interval.
... Day 4, Session 3 ...

Pakistan were pretty under-par with the ball in the second innings and even after having half the opposition out for just 117 runs, they failed to grab the opportunity to make inroads in the game. With the bat, so far Pakistan have been decent and have lost just one wicket but given the frailties in their middle order, a lot rides Imam-ul-Haq and Babar Azam, who has crossed 1000 Test runs as captain as both will be looking to not only make amends for the first innings but get their side safely into Day 5. The final session on Day 4 might prove to be an important one as it will set up the final day nicely. Join us at 3.15 pm IST (9.45 am GMT) to see if the hosts can tighten the screws on the opposition and close in on levelling the series.

Sri Lanka added on quick runs in the afternoon session as both Dhananjaya de Silva and Ramesh Mendis took on the bowlers and took the lead past 500 runs in no time. DDS though was run-out when it looked like there was a declaration coming and after the wicket, it did come. Asitha Fernando bowled well at the start and Sri Lanka produced a couple of half-chances but the pitch still looks decent for batting and the spinners have remained largely ineffective. The marathon man, Prabath Jayasuriya did get an important breakthrough and the hosts will now look to pick up a few more wickets before the end of Day 4.

The post-Lunch session on Day 4 has proved to be pretty even, to be honest, but the hosts are still well and truly on top as the opposition still needs 437 runs to win. Pakistan though have done well to keep the Lankan bowlers at bay for most of the session and are scoring briskly.

Ramesh Mendis tossed it up, full and on off. Imam-ul-Haq gets on his front foot and gets an inside edge onto the pads.
Imam-ul-Haq blocks this full delivery to point.
Fuller, outside off. Imam-ul-Haq defends it on his front foot.
Fuller, on the pads, Azam flicks it to mid-wicket. So, just a single off the over.
On the pads, tucked to the leg side.
Floated and full, outside off. Azam presses forward and blocks it back to the bowler.
It is full and on off. Azam hit it hard to mid on but finds the fielder.
On off, blocked out.
Fuller, on off, Imam-ul-Haq works it to long on for one.
Loopy ball, outside off, this one holds its line. Babar Azam tries to play for the turn but is comprehensively beaten.
Full and down leg. Imam-ul-Haq nudges it to square leg for a single. 50 is up for Pakistan.
Not a good follow-up delivery. It is full, angled down leg, Imam-ul-Haq clips it to fine leg for a brace.

FOUR! Imam-ul-Haq taking the charge here, although he gets very lucky. It is full and outside off, Imam-ul-Haq comes down the track and throws his bat at it. He looks to whack it down the track but it goes over the slip fielder off the outside edge and races away to the third man boundary.
Fuller, wide outside off. Babar Azam drives it to covers for a single.
Looped up, full and outside off, turning in off the surface. Babar Azam gets on his front foot and blocks it to the leg side off the inner half.
The skipper, Babar Azam walks in at number 3.

OUT! TAKEN! Prabath Jayasuriya gets the breakthrough and sends Abdullah Shafique back to the hut. This is tossed up on middle, Abdullah Shafique dances down the track to loft it over mid on, against the turn but the bat turns in his hand and he mistimes it. The ball goes high in the air and over wide of mid off, Dunith Wellalage runs back and sideways from mid off and takes an abosulte stunning catch over his shoulders, making sure he holds onto the ball when he hits the ground. Shafique will be very disappointed with that shot.
Commentary.Howout: c Dunith Wellalage b Prabath Jayasuriya

Commentary.Commentary: On middle, blocked out.
Flighted on middle, Abdullah Shafique makes room and uses his feet but drives it straight to mid off.
Floated on middle, angling in, Abdullah Shafique knocks it with his inner half to short leg.
Slightly short and on middle, Imam-ul-Haq tucks it from his back foot through square leg for one.
Tossed up full and on off, Imam-ul-Haq leans on and blocks it to the right of the bowler.
Full and on off, it is driven to mid on. A dot ball though.
A single now as this is worked down to mid on.
It is full, around middle and leg, this one skids through. Imam-ul-Haq's forward defense is beaten. He gets rapped on the pads. Ramesh Mendis appeals but the umpire denies. Going down leg.
This is outside off, Imam-ul-Haq cuts it to point but straight to the fielder.
Mendis serves it short, on off. Imam-ul-Haq remains solid in his defense.
This is on the stumps. Imam-ul-Haq defends it out.
On off, defended out. A maiden for Prabath Jayasuriya. His first one of the innings.
Floated and full, around off, skidding on. Abdullah Shafique gets it past short leg off the inner half.
This drifts into the pads, on a full length. Abdullah Shafique gets on his front foot and defends it to the right of the bowler off the inner half.
Fuller, sliding into the pads. Abdullah Shafique presses forward and blocks it out.
This is full and on the stumps. Abdullah Shafique blocks it out watchfully.
Fuller, on middle and leg, Abdullah Shafique comes down the track and flicks it to square leg.
This is full, outside off. Abdullah Shafique punches it through covers for a single.
Tossed up, on off. Abdullah Shafique defends it out.
Around off, blocked out.
Full and on fourth stump, Abdullah Shafique blocks it away.
Fuller and on off. Imam-ul-Haq comes down the track and looks to flick it away. It goes to the off side off the leading edge. They take one.
Tossed up, full and at the stumps. Abdullah Shafique hits it down to long on for a single.
Tossed up, outside off. Imam-ul-Haq defends it out.
Full and on off, blocked out.

Beautiful delivery! There is a huge appeal for stumping and the square leg umpire takes it upstairs. It is tossed up, outside off, and holds its line this time. Imam-ul-Haq stride forward to defend it out but does so inside the line. The ball zips past the outside edge. Niroshan Dickwella gathers the ball and is quick to clip the bails off. They appeal and the third umpire comes into play now. The UltraEdge shows no bat is involved. There is a small spike though but it is when the bat brushes the pads. The replays later show that Imam-ul-Haq had his back leg grounded and the final decision is not out.
Much fuller, around off. Imam-ul-Haq defends it watchfully.
It is flatter and full, outside off. Imam-ul-Haq cuts it late towards third man. They take two before the fielder cuts it out.
A loopy ball, outside off, turning in a touch. Imam-ul-Haq stays back and blocks it back to the bowler.
Darted on the pads, Imam-ul-Haq nudges it to square leg for a single.
Full and on off, blocked out watchfully.
Outside off, defended on the front foot.
This is angled into the pads, Imam-ul-Haq flicks it to short leg. The fielder collects the ball and throws it at the stumps. Although Imam-ul-Haq had his back foot on the ground.
On off, blocked out on the front foot.
Flighted and full, outside off. Imam-ul-Haq leans in and drives it uppishly towards covers. He does not go through with his shot and hence it does not carry
On the shorter side, turning into the pads, Abdullah Shafique hops back and dabs it down towards short leg.
Flighted, around off, Shafique pushes it towards cover.
On middle, kept out by Shafique.
Shafique tries to use his feet but Prabath Jayasuriya darts this one in. Shafique adjust well and keeps it out on the off side.
Tossed up, full and on middle, this is flicked away well in front of square on the leg side for a single.
Around off, Imam blocks it out.
A slight delay here. The umpire is having a bit of conversation with both the Pakistani batters in respect with a bit of time wasting.
Pushed through quicker on the leg stump, Abdullah Shafique stays back and knocks it to short leg.
Good running between the wickets here. This is drifted down the leg, Imam-ul-Haq whips it towards deep square leg while being slightly off balance. He times it really well and gets three runs.
On off, kept out.
Clever from Mendis. Imam-ul-Haq tries to use his feet again, Mendis sees this and pulls his length back a bit and on off, Imam-ul-Haq manages to block it.
Darts this one full and on middle, Imam-ul-Haq skips down and drives it to short mid-wicket.
Floated full and on off, Imam-ul-Haq uses his fee but does not get to the pitch of it, defends it out in the end.
Tossed up on middle, Abdullah Shafique comes forward and defends it to the off side.
Pushed through quicker and on off, Abdullah Shafique gets behind the line of it and blocks it out.
A bit short and on middle, Abdullah Shafique stays back and knocks it to the leg side.
Tossed up full and on off, Abdullah Shafique leans on and blocks it to the off side.
FOUR! Good shot! This is slightly over pitched around off, Abdullah Shafique dances down the track and drills it through extra covers for a boundary.
On middle , blocked out.
Quciker and flatter on middle, Imam-ul-Haq is solid in his defence.
Better from Mendis. This is slower and full, on middle, Imam-ul-Haq strides forward and defends it well.
Mendis needs to correct his length here. This is short again and on middle, Imam-ul-Haq tucks it away through mid-wicket for a brace.

FOUR! Poor from Mendis. He bowls this short again and outside off, Imam-ul-Haq punches it off his back foot past backward point for a boundary. There was a slight hesitation from the fielder there and he cannot stop it.
Slightly short and on off, Abdullah Shafique stays back and works it through mid-wicket for a single.
Ramesh Mendis starts with a short delivery and outside off, Imam-ul-Haq cuts it through cover-point for one.
Spin from both ends now as Ramesh Mendis comes on to bowl.
Tossed up on middle and leg, Abdullah Shafique blocks it out.
Floated full and on middle, Abdullah Shafique uses his feet and drills it to the right of the bowler where Prabath Jayasuriya makes a half stop.
On off, kept out.
FOUR! Half a chance! This is flatter and quicker down the leg, Abdullah Shafique flicks it and the ball goes just past the diving leg slip fielder and towards the fine leg fence for a boundary.
Floated on off, Abdullah Shafique gets to the pitch of it and pushes it back to the bowler.
Tossed up around off, Imam-ul-Haq steps out and eases it past short mid-wicket and towards long on for one.
On the pads, this is flicked away to fine leg for a single.
Good length, on middle and leg, Imam nudges it onto the leg side.
Full and straight, Imam digs it out towards cover-point.
Keeps it around the top of off, Imam defends it towards short cover.
back of a length, over middle, Imam-ul-Haq gets behind the line of the ball to make the block.
On a good length, a bit of width on offer, Imam hangs back and taps it towards point.
Flatter and around off, kept out on the off side.
PEACH! Prabath Jayasuriya with a ripper of a delivery, nicely flighted, full and on off stump. The ball just grips and turns away sharply, leaving Shafique completely bamboozled.
Holds it back a touch and drifts it onto middle and leg, Shafique blocks it out.
A tad shorter and on the pads, Imam goes on the back foot and turns it past square leg for a single.
Flighted, around off, Imam blocks it out.
FOUR! Some positive intent now from Imam-ul-Haq. This is tossed up on middle, Imam dances down the track and lofts it over the bowler's head for a boundary.

FOUR! Short and punished! Asitha Fernando goes for another short ball but this one sits up nicely around leg stump, Abdullah Shafique swivels and pulls it powerfully into the backward square leg fence. That will ease Shafique's nerves a bit.
Full and on off, pushed back firmly towards the bowler.

TAKEN! Oh, wait! It's a no ball! Asitha Fernando has committed the cardinal sin and Abdullah Shafique is left off the hook. This is shorter and on the body, Shafique awkwardly tries to fend it away but ends up playing it uppishly to the right of short leg. The fielder over there shows great reflexes to grab it but it doesn't matter. On watching the replay, the catch too might have not been a clean one but for now Shafique will continue his stay. Well, Asitha Fernando does not have to blame himself, as the replays show that the ball had bouced before going into the palms of short leg fielder. Although, it wasn't a clean replay. It looks like most of it would've come down on the soft signal.
Excellent from Fernando, touching 140 KPH now and hitting the bat hard. On off, Shafique manages to keep it out on the off side.
Length this time, on off, Shafique defends it late and with soft hands as well.
hard length, around off, Shafique looks to defend off the front foot and once again gets an inside edge that goes down towards short leg.
Fernando with a really well-directed bumper now. Over middle and leg and with some good heat behind it. Abdullah Shafique does well to duck under it in time.
Loops it up a bit and delivers it around middle and off, Imam-ul-Haq presses forward to defend.
Turning it in from around off, defended off the front foot.
Around off, Imam keeps it out.
This one comes on with the arm. On off and angling in sharply, Shafique gets an inside edge past the man at first slip and gets off the mark with a single, also survives a pair in the process.
Better from the bowler. Gives it a lot more air and bowls it fuller around off, Shafique makes a watchful block.

Prabath Jayasuriya starts off with a loosener and Imam-ul-Haq is off the mark right away. This is shorter and outside off, Imam taps it off the back foot through point for a single and with that Pakistan are underway in the chase.
It will be Prabath Jayasuriya to share the new ball.
A maiden to start with from Asitha Fernando! Pitches it up on off, Shafique makes yet another solid block off the front foot.
A bit of aggression from Asitha Fernando, bangs it in over leg stump with the ball angling further down leg. Shafique manages to duck under it.
Angles this one in a bit fuller and onto middle and leg, Shafique presents a dead bat at it.
A touch fuller, keeping it around off and there's movement again. This time there's a solid block off the front foot by Shafique.
Around the top of off, Shafique looks to just stick out his blade and defend it out but gets a thick inside edge. Luckily for him, the ball goes back on to hit the pads and not the stumps.
Fernando starts off with a gentle-paced delivery, full and outside off, with a hint of swing into the right-hander. Abdullah Shafique shoulders arms at it.
